sources.title: Sonar Pro — retained Sonar model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh direct Markdown re-open on October 27 identifies sonar-pro, gives a 200K context, standard non-reasoning behavior and retrieval capabilities, and warns that Agent API replaced Sonar. It states no nominal total or activated parameter count and no named base-model lineage.

sources.title: Perplexity blog index — Introducing the Sonar Pro API
sources.evidence: Direct first-party index HTML pairs Introducing the Sonar Pro API by Perplexity with time datetime 2025-01-21T00:00:00.000Z. It corroborates the launch day independently of search-engine publication metadata.

sources.title: Perplexity launch announcement — official X post 1881779310840984043
sources.evidence: Direct X syndication JSON identifies the Perplexity business account perplexity_ai, timestamp 2025-01-21T19:02:04.000Z, announces Sonar API and says a Pro version with deeper functionality is being offered. Canonical post: https://x.com/perplexity_ai/status/1881779310840984043.

sources.title: Introducing the Sonar Pro API — official Dutch translation
sources.evidence: Complete indexed primary article text accessed through web search; direct HTML retrieval was blocked. The launch introduces Sonar and Sonar Pro and says the latter becomes generally available to all developers today; describes longer context and more retrieval. The separately accessed official index supplies January 21, 2025. This establishes historical public availability, not current operation.

sources.title: Sonar model range
sources.evidence: Retained first-party model comparison places Sonar Pro alongside Sonar in the Sonar range, under search, separate from Sonar Reasoning Pro and Sonar Deep Research. It does not identify Sonar Pro as a pricing-only tier of the identical Sonar checkpoint.

sources.title: Perplexity API Terms of Service
sources.evidence: January 23, 2026 terms expressly cover Sonar by Perplexity. Sections 2.1 and 3.1 grant restricted hosted-service access and retain model intellectual property with Perplexity or its licensors; there is no checkpoint distribution grant. Supports a proprietary API classification, not an SPDX weight-license assertion.

sources.title: Sonar Media & Attachments
sources.evidence: Direct retained Markdown gives exact model="sonar-pro" examples for text plus image input and PDF file_url input, with URL or base64 transport. Supported files include PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT and RTF. Response images and videos are retrieved media assets; they do not establish image/video generation or video input.

sources.title: Pro Search for Sonar Pro — quickstart
sources.evidence: Exact sonar-pro examples enable optional Pro Search using stream=true and web_search_options.search_type="pro". It documents multi-step reasoning, dynamic tool execution and thought streaming, compared with the standard fast mode and single fixed search. Non-streaming requests revert to standard behavior.

sources.title: Pro Search built-in tool capabilities
sources.evidence: Explicitly states that the model decides which tools to use and when. Built-ins are web_search and fetch_url_content; executions appear in reasoning_steps. Custom tools cannot be registered. This supports model-chosen built-in tool use, not arbitrary user-defined function calling.

sources.title: Perplexity API changelog
sources.evidence: January 2025 announces Sonar and Sonar Pro APIs; November 2025 announces Pro Search general availability for Sonar Pro with automated tools and multi-step reasoning. April 2025 adds image uploads and September 2025 file attachments. These are later capabilities of the same named API, not launch-day specifications.

sources.title: Sonar to Agent API migration overview
sources.evidence: States support for Sonar Chat Completions ended September 27, 2026. Synchronous and streaming requests are gradually reformulated into Agent API calls; async Sonar is unsupported. Continued compatibility therefore does not establish continued inference on the original Sonar Pro model.

sources.title: Agent API vs Sonar benchmarks
sources.evidence: Fresh direct Markdown re-open on October 27. The later comparison explicitly labels Sonar Pro retired and measurements pre-retirement baselines. Its columns are BrowseComp/DSQA accuracy and request cost, not total or activated parameters. Mapping Sonar Pro to Agent API fast is a replacement recommendation, not checkpoint lineage.

sources.title: Third-Party Models & Terms
sources.evidence: Fresh direct HTML re-open on October 27. The November 25, 2025 legal table says Sonar models; its footnote names Sonar as a Perplexity fine-tune of Llama 3.1 70B. It never names Sonar Pro or binds that API model to the base. This generic family statement is insufficient to resolve the variant, especially alongside the separate Llama 3.3 announcement.

sources.title: Meet new Sonar
sources.evidence: Fresh original English HTML at https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/meet-new-sonar accessed directly on October 27, alongside the indexed en-GB article. It explicitly says Sonar was further trained from Llama 3.3 70B and compares it with Llama 3.3 70B Instruct. Sonar Pro is not named. This supports basic Sonar nominal lineage, not a Pro count. It is JMIR reference 20 and OPENXRD reference 100.

sources.title: A good teacher meets the student where they are — Perplexity JOLT research
sources.evidence: Fresh direct official Korean article re-open on October 27; the research index dates it October 21, 2026. JOLT experiments name DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B-Instruct and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct. Sonar Pro is not named, so these later training comparisons supply no total or active count for this record.

sources.title: Perplexity Research publication index
sources.evidence: Fresh primary publication-index re-open on October 27, followed by JOLT and WANDR research. Bounded searches covered exact Sonar Pro/sonar-pro with parameters, parameter count, 70B, Llama, active parameters, activated parameters and later research tables, including perplexity.ai, research.perplexity.ai, docs.perplexity.ai and arxiv.org. No applicable developer nominal count, explicit Pro base-model relationship or research-team active-count convention was established. Research-table leads were traced individually in s18-s20; this is not a claim of exhaustive absence.

sources.title: Introducing the Sonar Pro API — original English URL
sources.evidence: Fresh original English HTML accessed directly on October 27 (HTTP 200), resolving the earlier fetch failure. Dated January 21, 2025, it introduces Sonar and Sonar Pro separately, with more citations and a larger context for Pro. It reports SimpleQA results but no nominal total, active count or named base checkpoint.

sources.title: Evaluating Web Retrieval-Assisted Large Language Models With and Without Whitelisting for Evidence-Based Neurology
sources.publisher: Masanneck et al. / Journal of Medical Internet Research
sources.evidence: Fresh original article accessed. Methods say Sonar and Sonar-Pro use Llama 3.3 70B for March 18, 2025 API runs. Reference 20 resolves only to Perplexity Meet New Sonar (s14), which does not name Pro; no independent Pro lineage or parameter measurement is supplied. The clinical study is original performance research but its model-size attribution is a secondary, insufficiently traced claim. No active parameter count appears.

sources.title: OPENXRD: a comprehensive benchmark framework for LLM/MLLM XRD question answering
sources.publisher: Vosoughi et al. / Royal Society of Chemistry
sources.evidence: Original publisher article text accessed through indexed search; direct HTML/PDF requests returned 403. Table 1 explicitly lists perplexity/sonar-pro as 70B without an estimate marker. Its caption defines total/active notation only for MoE entries; Pro has no separate active value. Section 3.1.1 cites reference 99, the Pro capabilities page now redirected to migration docs, and reference 100, Meet New Sonar (s14). Reference 99 describes context/citations and reference 100 identifies basic Sonar Llama 3.3 70B. No Pro-specific size derivation is given. Preserve this later research claim as unverified rather than promoting its untraced 70B to a developer specification.

sources.title: InfiAgent: An Infinite-Horizon Framework for General-Purpose Autonomous Agents
sources.publisher: Yu et al. / Association for Computational Linguistics
sources.evidence: Fresh original ACL 2026 paper accessed. Appendix Table 1, PDF page 9, lists sonar-pro with Params (B) 70. The caption explicitly says parameter values are estimates based on public reports, without a model-specific supporting reference. This is another unverified total estimate, not an independently established Sonar Pro nominal specification; the table has no activated-parameter column.

sources.title: WANDR benchmark: Evaluating research agents that must search wide and deep
sources.evidence: Fresh direct original research article accessed, dated July 14, 2026, following the Agent API benchmark link. Describes agent evaluation and precision/recall metrics; it does not name Sonar Pro or supply total/active parameter counts for it. This later research does not resolve the parameter fields.

name.note: Official product/model spelling; exact API identifier sonar-pro.

developer.note: Perplexity publishes and operates this named API model. This does not attribute undisclosed underlying checkpoints to a particular base-model developer.

family.note: Normalize to the official Sonar model range; Sonar Pro is a member, not its own family.

release_date.note: Earliest public general availability verified for the exact Sonar Pro API name. Replaces unsupported January 1, 2024. Private partner use, earlier llama-3.1-sonar variants and later Pro Search rollout are separate events.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is the hosted API under restricted service terms; no Sonar Pro checkpoint release is offered in the reviewed primary release/model materials. Open availability of a possible base model does not make these served weights open.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted Sonar Pro offering. The API terms retain model rights and grant service access; no inference of a separately released weight license.

parameters_b.note: No supported nominal total is established for Sonar Pro. JMIR and OPENXRD state 70B, but their traced references establish only basic Sonar lineage or Pro API capabilities; InfiAgent labels its 70B value an estimate from public reports. A developer-named Pro base relationship would support nominal inference, but neither the original launch nor the retained model page supplies one.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh separate searches and later developer/research comparisons establish no nominal active count for Sonar Pro. OPENXRD uses total/active notation for MoE rows but gives Pro only 70B; InfiAgent has one estimated Params column. Neither supplies a Pro active-count convention. Do not equate an unverified total with active parameters or infer a dense architecture.

architecture.note: No exact Sonar Pro network topology is established. Reviewed later first-party comparison/training research and searched first-party interpretability disclosures; related Sonar and research experiment model architectures cannot be transferred. Search/reasoning orchestration describes API behavior, not neural topology.

context_window.note: Retain nominal 200K-token context from the exact legacy model page. It is a last-documented Sonar Pro limit, not proof that the replacement Agent API uses the same window.

modalities.note: Exact sonar-pro image and PDF examples support API input capability; no claim that PDF handling is native to one checkpoint. Returned image/video search assets do not imply generative output modalities. These later-documented capabilities are not asserted as available at launch.

reasoning.note: Capability exists in optional streamed Pro Search, documented from November 2025. Standard fast Sonar Pro is explicitly non-reasoning. True records the named API capability and must not imply every request reasons or that the base checkpoint is a separately disclosed reasoning model.

tool_call.note: Optional Pro Search lets the model choose built-in web_search and fetch_url_content and chain them. This goes beyond deterministic retrieval; arbitrary custom functions cannot be registered. Standard fast search alone would not establish this flag.

description.value: Search model for cited answers, with image and document input and optional Pro Search reasoning and web tools.
description.note: Replaces vague comparative quality claims with documented behavior; specifies optional reasoning/tool mode. API retirement is explained in notes.

patch.notes: Sonar Pro was publicly released on January 21, 2025. The standard fast mode is non-reasoning; the reasoning and tool-use flags refer to optional streamed Pro Search, documented from November 2025, where the model selects built-in web search and URL fetching. Custom functions cannot be registered. PDF input reflects API document handling, while returned image/video URLs are retrieved assets. Total parameters remain unverified; active parameters and network architecture are undisclosed. Published 70B claims lack a traced Sonar Pro lineage source; the documented Llama 3.3 70B model is Sonar. Sonar Chat Completions support ended September 27, 2026; synchronous and streaming requests are gradually translated to Agent API calls. Specifications here describe the retained Sonar Pro documentation, not verified current inference on the original model.

summary: Parameter re-audit: keep explicit null total and active counts and clear parameters_source. Trace the JMIR/OPENXRD 70B claims to basic Sonar lineage and Pro capabilities rather than a Pro size disclosure; InfiAgent explicitly calls its 70B value an estimate. Reopen the original English launch successfully and check retained documentation, legal lineage, JOLT, WANDR and later Agent API comparisons. No supported nominal total or active-count convention is established. Preserve the other 12 field assessments and their earlier release, capability and retirement corrections.
